question: In the synthetic 4,000-person extract supplied with the task, what is the average effect on the treated (ATT) of enrolling in the voluntary 1976-77 job-training program (the enrolment indicator in the file) on participants' 1978 earnings (re78), under the assumption that enrolment is independent of potential outcomes given eleven pre-program covariates (age, educ, married, urban, region, children, health_limit, re74, re75, unemp74, unemp75), and is that effect smaller in magnitude than an equivalence margin of 10% of participants' mean pre-program (1975) earnings?
hypotheses: H1 (primary): the ATT on re78 is zero; two-sided test at 5%. The paper reports the point estimate and 95% confidence interval and never states 'no effect' on the basis of a non-rejection alone.

H1b (equivalence, primary): the ATT on re78 lies within (-M, +M), where M = 0.10 x the mean of re75 among participants. M depends only on a pre-program variable; the Data RA computes it at data preparation, records it as a data-prep run metric and logs it before the design gate, so it is fixed before any outcome is examined. Test: two one-sided tests at 5% (equivalently, the 90% CI inside the margin). The 10% margin is the crew's own choice of a smallest effect of interest, not a convention from the literature; no external benchmark is claimed to apply to this synthetic extract. Because 1975 earnings may be depressed just before enrolment, the Data RA also records, outcome-blind, a precision proxy (the standard error the ATT would have if re78 had re75's variance) so the reader can see in advance whether H1b is testable. If H1b is not supported, the paper reports the smallest symmetric margin that the 90% interval would satisfy and does not change M. Price year: the brief does not state one; earnings are reported in the file's nominal units and the paper says so. Only if H1b is supported may the paper say the effect is smaller than M.

H2 (secondary family): the ATTs on re79, employed78, hours78, benefits78 and wellbeing78. Each is reported with its estimate, a Romano-Wolf familywise-adjusted p-value over these five outcomes, and simultaneous (max-t) 95% confidence intervals; uncorrected p-values are shown next to adjusted ones. An outcome counts as 'detected' only if its Romano-Wolf adjusted p-value is below 0.05; the max-t intervals are reported descriptively for what each outcome rules out.
contribution: A pre-specified observational evaluation in which the estimand, the conditioning set, the closed list of outcomes and their multiple-testing corrections, and an equivalence margin are all fixed while every outcome is still unexamined, with every analysed outcome reported. The data are synthetic; no claim is made about any real program.

tasks.title: Prior work on evaluating job-training programs with observational data; methods for selection on observables

question.summary: Question ready after Reviewer rounds; see reviews/question-r*.

outcomes.not_analysed: survey_q01-survey_q20: their timing relative to the program is not documented, so they can be neither confounders nor outcomes with confidence. They are not used as covariates and not analysed as outcomes; this is stated as a limitation.
outcomes.relative_effect_denominator: The ATT as a percentage of participants' estimated counterfactual mean re78 (mean re78 of participants minus the ATT), not the non-participant mean.
